tools.name: garmin_get_activities
tools.description: List Garmin activity summaries (runs, rides, swims, hikes, strength...) in a date window: sport, duration, distance, avg/max HR, pace/power averages. Use to locate a session before pulling detail. Example: garmin_get_activities({ start_date: "2026-06-03", end_date: "2026-06-10" }). For per-lap / per-rep analysis go to garmin_get_activity_file (full .fit) or garmin_get_activity_details - summaries only carry averages. Data arrives via Garmin webhooks, so an activity finished minutes ago may not be here yet; widen the window by a day on each side when hunting "today's" session (date labels are user-local). For "what did I do this week"-style totals do NOT sum this list: the same physical session is also returned by strava_get_activities and intervals_get_activities, so totaling them triple-counts (e.g. a 38km week reads as 113km). Use get_analytics_summary (weekly_volume.km / by_sport_km) for deduped weekly distance/hours/load.

start_date.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (user-local). For 'last N days' use today minus N-1.

end_date.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (user-local), inclusive

tools.name: garmin_get_activity
tools.description: Get detailed Garmin activity by ID: summary stats, splits, HR zones, average/max power. NOTE: Garmin's activity-summary push does NOT include Training Effect, anaerobic TE, Intensity Factor, TSS, or training/exercise load — those live in the .fit session message, so use garmin_get_activity_file for any of them. Use this tool when you have a specific activity_id (e.g. from a webhook) and need splits/HR-zone depth beyond what get_activity_detail provides. For per-rep analysis on structured workouts, also prefer garmin_get_activity_file (parses the .fit). Example: garmin_get_activity({ id: "18923456789" }).

tools.name: garmin_get_daily_summaries
tools.description: Get Garmin per-day rollups: steps, active/resting calories, intensity minutes, stress avg, body battery (start/end/min/max), resting HR, floors climbed. Use when reviewing all-day load and recovery state outside of structured workouts (e.g. "is today a rest day?" body battery + RHR + stress paint that picture). Example: garmin_get_daily_summaries({ start_date: "2026-05-01", end_date: "2026-05-07" }).

tools.name: garmin_get_sleep
tools.description: Get Garmin sleep records: total/deep/light/REM/awake minutes, sleep score (0-100), restlessness, average SpO2, average HRV during sleep. Use when Garmin is the athlete's primary sleep source, or to cross-check Oura/WHOOP when results disagree. Quote the raw stage minutes + HRV, NOT just the sleep score. FRESHNESS: each record's date is the WAKE date; if the latest record's date predates the athlete's current local date, they have NO data for last night - do not present it as "last night" or current. Example: garmin_get_sleep({ start_date: "2026-05-01", end_date: "2026-05-07" }).

tools.name: garmin_get_body_composition
tools.description: Get Garmin Index Scale body comp readings: weight (kg), body fat %, muscle mass (kg), bone mass, body water %, BMI. Use when reviewing body comp trends and the athlete uses a Garmin scale (most don't - Withings is more common). Example: garmin_get_body_composition({ start_date: "2026-04-01", end_date: "2026-05-07" }).

tools.name: garmin_get_stress
tools.description: Get Garmin all-day stress data: average / max stress score (0-100), high/medium/low/rest minutes, body battery curve (start/end/charge/drain). Use when assessing autonomic load on top of training. Body battery dropping fast on a rest day = something else is taxing the athlete (sleep debt, illness, work). Example: garmin_get_stress({ start_date: "2026-05-01", end_date: "2026-05-07" }).

tools.name: garmin_get_pulse_ox
tools.description: Get Garmin SpO2 readings: continuous and on-demand pulse oximetry (avg/min %). Use when investigating altitude exposure, sleep-disordered breathing signals, or unexplained recovery dips (SpO2 dropping below 90% during sleep is a flag). Example: garmin_get_pulse_ox({ start_date: "2026-05-01", end_date: "2026-05-07" }).

tools.name: garmin_get_heart_rate
tools.description: Get Garmin daily HR series: resting HR, max HR, average HR over 24h. Use for RHR trend reviews (is RHR drifting up = stress/illness/overreaching, drifting down = adaptation). Pair with garmin_get_hrv for fuller autonomic picture. Example: garmin_get_heart_rate({ start_date: "2026-04-01", end_date: "2026-05-07" }).

tools.name: garmin_get_respiration
tools.description: Get Garmin respiration data: average / lowest / highest breaths-per-minute over the day, continuous if device supports it. Use when investigating illness onset (resp rate elevated >1-2 bpm above baseline is an early warning) or sleep quality. Example: garmin_get_respiration({ start_date: "2026-05-01", end_date: "2026-05-07" }).

tools.name: garmin_get_user_metrics
tools.description: Get Garmin's computed user metrics: VO2 max (running and cycling separately), fitness age, lactate threshold HR/pace if estimated. Use when answering capability questions ("what's my current VO2 max?") or sanity-checking goal pacing - Garmin VO2 max trend is a useful long-term fitness indicator. Example: garmin_get_user_metrics({ start_date: "2026-04-01", end_date: "2026-05-07" }).

tools.name: garmin_get_hrv
tools.description: Get HRV (heart rate variability) summaries from Garmin (weekly avg, last night HRV, status, baseline range). Key metric for recovery and readiness assessment.

tools.name: garmin_get_activity_details
tools.description: Get detailed Garmin activity records (laps, HR zones, training effect, power, running dynamics, GPS) for every activity in a date window - NOTE it takes a date RANGE, not an activity id, and returns a list. Use for structured-session depth when you don't have an activity id or the .fit; for full-resolution per-rep work prefer garmin_get_activity_file. Example: garmin_get_activity_details({ start_date: "2026-06-09", end_date: "2026-06-10" }) to dissect this morning's intervals. Keep the window tight (1-3 days) - payloads are large.

start_date.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (user-local). Keep the window tight (1-3 days) - payloads are large.

end_date.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (user-local), inclusive

tools.name: garmin_get_skin_temps
tools.description: Get Garmin skin temperature deviation (measured during sleep, in °C from baseline). Use when investigating illness onset (+0.3°C deviation often precedes symptoms by 24-48h), menstrual phase tracking, or unexplained recovery dips. Watch-only feature - not all Garmin devices report it. Example: garmin_get_skin_temps({ start_date: "2026-05-01", end_date: "2026-05-07" }).

tools.name: garmin_get_health_snapshot
tools.description: Get Garmin health snapshot data (2-min on-demand readings: HR, HRV, stress, SpO2, respiration)

tools.name: garmin_get_move_iq
tools.description: Get Move IQ auto-detected activities from Garmin (walking, running, cycling detected automatically)

tools.name: garmin_get_activity_file
tools.description: Get parsed .fit file data for a single Garmin activity (sessions, laps, lengths for pool swims, per-sample time-series with HR/power/cadence/speed/altitude/GPS). REQUIRED whenever the user asks about per-rep stroke rate, SWOLF, cadence, efficiency, or anything sub-lap — the summary endpoints don't carry that. ALSO REQUIRED for Training Effect (aerobic + anaerobic), Intensity Factor, TSS, and training/exercise load: these are NOT in the activity-summary push (garmin_get_activity returns them as null) — they live here in the session message (`sessions[0]`: total_training_effect, total_anaerobic_training_effect, intensity_factor, training_stress_score, training_load_peak). Pool swims: per-length stroke counts and swim_stroke type live in `lengths`. Accepts a Garmin activity ID; if you only have the Strava ID for the same workout, pass it anyway and we'll match to the Garmin row by date+sport+distance. Garmin pushes the .fit via webhook within ~5 min of an activity completing, so CALL THIS FIRST for recent activities; only fall back to summary/lap data if this tool actually returns 'no file stored'. Returns 1 Hz samples downsampled to one point per `sample_seconds` (default 30s). Use `sample_seconds: 1` for full resolution but expect a large payload. Each lap carries a `lap_trigger` (manual = athlete pressed the lap button = a real interval marker; distance/time = the watch's automatic auto-lap = NOT a rep); when the laps are pure auto-laps the response includes a top-level `lapStructureWarning` - honor it and do NOT narrate auto-laps as the workout's reps.

id.description: Garmin activity ID (Strava ID also accepted; auto-resolves to the matching Garmin activity)

sample_seconds.description: Downsample interval in seconds (default 30). Set to 1 for full 1 Hz resolution.

tools.name: garmin_list_activity_files
tools.description: List Garmin activities that have a parsed .fit file available. Returns activityId + start time + session summary for each. Use garmin_get_activity_file to fetch the full time-series for a specific activity.

tools.name: search_research
tools.description: Search for sports science research and evidence-based answers. Use for training principles, injury mechanisms, nutrition science, recovery protocols, supplement efficacy, and exercise physiology questions. Returns an answer with citations from peer-reviewed sources.

tools.name: food_log_get
tools.description: Query food logs by date range across all sources (manual entries plus Cronometer / MyFitnessPal via Terra). Returns individual entries plus daily macro totals. Use to review what the user ate, track daily nutrition, or analyze eating patterns.

start_date.description: Start date in YYYY-MM-DD format (defaults to today)

end_date.description: End date in YYYY-MM-DD format (defaults to today)

timezone.description: IANA timezone for correct day boundaries (e.g. 'America/New_York'). Pass the user's timezone so date queries align with their local calendar.

tools.name: food_log_entry
tools.description: Log a food entry with estimated macronutrients. Use when the user describes what they ate (text or photo). Always estimate macros even if approximate.

description.description: Human-readable description of the meal (e.g., '2 eggs, toast with butter, and coffee')

food_items.description: Individual food items with per-item macro breakdown

name.description: Food item name with quantity (e.g., '2 scrambled eggs')

logged_at.description: ISO datetime when the meal was eaten (defaults to now)

tools.name: get_training_trends
tools.description: Get pre-computed training trends across all connected platforms. Returns training volume (sessions, duration, distance by type, week-over-week comparison), recovery metrics (HRV values and trend, RHR values and trend), and sleep summary. Much faster than pulling raw data from each platform individually. Use this for quick trend checks before diving into detailed data from specific platforms.

days.description: Number of days to analyze (default 14, max 28)

tools.name: coaching_note_create
tools.description: Save a coaching insight, analysis result, or observation for future reference. Use this to avoid repeating analyses, track trends you've spotted, record milestones, or flag concerns. Your future self will thank you.

category.description: Type of note: trend_insight (pattern you spotted), milestone (PR, goal reached), concern (overtraining, injury risk, illness signal)

content.description: The insight or analysis to save (be specific - include numbers, dates, and context)

data_range.description: Date range this note covers, e.g. '2026-02-24 to 2026-03-02'

tools.name: coaching_note_get
tools.description: Retrieve past coaching notes - your previous analyses, insights, and observations. Check these before doing a new analysis to avoid repeating work and to build on previous findings.

since_days.description: Only return notes from the last N days

tools.name: get_analytics_summary
tools.description: Get cached analytics summary. Returns PMC (CTL/ATL/TSB), weekly volume, wellness trends. Fast DB query. Includes data_freshness - if stale (>24h), prefer live integration tools for current data. Best for historical analysis and trends. weekly_volume is DEDUPED across providers (km, by_sport_km, hours, load, sessions) - this is the authoritative source for weekly distance/hours/load; never sum the per-provider list tools yourself.

tools.name: get_pmc_status
tools.description: Get current PMC status - CTL (fitness), ATL (fatigue), TSB (form), trend, form interpretation. Fast DB query. Includes data_freshness - if stale, warn the user and suggest syncing on the analytics dashboard.

tools.name: get_daily_metrics
tools.description: Get daily_metrics rows over a window. One-stop call returning PMC (CTL/ATL/TSB), wellness (HRV, RHR, sleep, weight), composite scores (recovery_score, readiness_verdict, injury_risk_index), load math (acwr, monotony, strain_foster), z-scores vs personal 60d baseline, and detected anomalies. Prefer this over stitching multiple tools when you need a multi-day picture.

tools.name: get_readiness_today
tools.description: Should the athlete train hard today? Returns recovery_score (0-100, pure physio: HRV z, RHR z, sleep, sleep debt), readiness_score (0-100, training-readiness: recovery + TSB + ACWR + monotony drag), readiness_verdict (go_hard|steady|easy|rest), the contributing drivers, AND adjusted_zones — today's HR and power zones dynamically nudged ±5% from the user's static LTHR/FTP based on HRV/RHR vs 60-day baseline (Morpheus-style). Prefer readiness_score when answering 'can I train hard today'; recovery_score tells you how the body is, readiness tells you what the training context says on top. Use adjusted_zones when telling the user what HR/power targets to hit TODAY; use the static zones on activity_metrics for historical comparison. FRESHNESS: the as_of field is the wake-date of the latest row; if as_of predates the athlete's current local date this is NOT last night's recovery (device off or unsynced) - do not present it as "last night" or current.

tools.name: get_injury_risk
tools.description: Current injury risk index (0-100) with contributing drivers (acwr_high, ramp_rate_high, monotony_high, hrv_decline, sleep_debt_severe) and the underlying numbers. Includes 14-day trend so you can see if risk is rising. Use whenever the user mentions niggles, fatigue accumulation, or asks 'am I overtraining?'.

tools.name: get_anomalies
tools.description: Detected outliers in HRV, RHR, and sleep score over the last N days vs personal 60d baseline. Sorted by severity (|z-score|). Use this proactively at the start of a check-in to surface 'anything weird?' before the user has to ask.

tools.name: get_load_balance
tools.description: Acute:chronic workload ratio (ACWR), Foster monotony, Foster strain, ramp rate, and sport load split (ride/run/strength/etc.) over the window. ACWR sweet spot is 0.8-1.3; monotony >2 is a warning sign. Use when discussing training load distribution, taper, or whether the athlete is ramping safely.

tools.name: get_power_curve
tools.description: Mean-max power curve for cycling over a window. Returns best avg power held for 1, 5, 10, 20, 30, 45, 60, 90 minutes. Note: derived from per-activity averages (not stream sampling), so values are conservative lower bounds. Use for FTP/CP discussion, peak fitness comparison, identifying training gaps at specific durations.

tools.name: get_pace_curve
tools.description: Mean-max pace curve for running. Returns best avg pace (seconds per km) sustained for each duration bucket. Use for threshold pace discussion, race-time prediction context, and identifying training gaps.

tools.name: get_activity_detail
tools.description: Detailed analytics for a single activity: training load, NP, HR + power zone breakdown, weather-adjusted values, plus a `derived_metrics` block with Intensity Factor, Variability Index, Efficiency Factor and aerobic decoupling (IF/VI/EF are computed from NP/power/HR + the athlete's FTP/threshold when the provider didn't store them; decoupling passes through from the source), and any duplicate rows from other providers merged into this canonical activity. For strength sessions (Hevy, or Garmin when the .fit carries set detail) the activity also carries `total_volume` (kg), `total_sets`, and a `strength_exercises` breakdown with each exercise name, its working sets and volume, and every set's load/reps/RPE/type - use this for lift-by-lift coaching ('how did my squats look?') instead of asking the athlete to re-type their sets. For endurance sessions the activity may carry `splits` (per-KILOMETRE: distanceMeters, durationSec, avgPaceSecPerKm, avgHr) and, on lap-capable Apple Health builds, `laps` (the watch's own work/recovery boundaries: index, kind, startSec, durationSec, distanceMeters, avgPaceSecPerKm, avgHr). PREFER `laps` for per-REP structure - they are the true boundaries the watch recorded and align to the reps even when the reps sit off the kilometre marks; `splits` are the per-km view. Apple Health runs from recent mobile builds populate these on-device plus an `hr_zones` breakdown, so an Apple-Health-only athlete's intervals are readable here, not only via a screenshot; don't reconstruct per-rep pace by hand when `laps` is present. `splits`/`laps` are pulled from whichever provider copy of the session actually recorded them (a run tracked by both Garmin and Strava usually has its per-km splits on the Strava copy), so they show up here even when the canonical row is the split-less Garmin one - `splits_source` / `laps_source` name the provider each came from; cite that app, don't assume it matches the activity's main source. This returns avg/max HR plus the time-in-zone SUMMARY, not the second-by-second trace; for the raw HR/pace/power signal call the provider's stream tool (strava_get_activity_streams, or garmin_get_activity_file for a full-resolution .fit). Use when discussing a specific session ('how was my Tuesday tempo?', 'why did that long run feel so hard?'). Provide source_activity_id when known, otherwise pass date (and optionally source) to look up by day.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD if id is not known

tools.name: get_dedupe_clusters
tools.description: Show which activities were merged across providers (e.g. the same run captured by both Strava and Garmin). Returns canonical rows used in PMC/sport split/curves and the duplicate rows that were folded in. Use this when the user says 'I see only one run but I did two' or when explaining why aggregated metrics don't match a provider's raw count.

tools.name: get_performance_estimates
tools.description: Full performance analysis: FTP, Critical Power (CP), W' (anaerobic work capacity), threshold pace, race equivalents, power profile analysis (strengths/weaknesses across sprint-to-endurance spectrum rated as strong/moderate/weak with athlete archetype classification), Coggan 7-zone power zones with watt ranges, and prioritized training recommendations targeting identified limiters with specific session examples. Use when discussing fitness level, race targets, training zones, 'what should I work on?', or power profile.

tools.name: analyze_dose_response
tools.description:
Mine the athlete's historical data for dose-response patterns: when stimulus X happened, how did response metric Y change vs their 14-day baseline over the next 1-2 days? Bins events by dose magnitude (low/med/high tertiles) and reports median response delta + sample size per bin. Use this to find an athlete's personal sweet spot and tolerance for a given training stimulus.

Stimulus types:
- high_intensity_session: single sessions with IF >= 0.85 (or top-quartile training load if no IF). Response window: day +1.
- long_endurance: sessions >= 90 min duration with IF < 0.80. Response window: day +1.
- strength: strength/weight training sessions. Response window: day +1.
- weekly_volume: total weekly training load (one event per week). Response window: days +1 and +2 after week end.
- back_to_back_hard: two consecutive days each with daily load >= 60 TSS. Response window: days +1 and +2 after the second day.

Response metrics (each requires data from a connected source):
- hrv (RMSSD, ms) - higher is better
- rhr (resting HR, bpm) - lower is better (sign auto-normalized)
- sleep_score (0-100) - higher is better
- readiness (Oura/WHOOP recovery score) - higher is better
- tsb (form) - higher is better

Important: this is observational n=1 analysis. Confounders are NOT controlled. Always report sample size when narrating to the user, and flag bins with n<5 as too thin. Treat patterns as discussion starters, not physiological laws. If the tool returns status=insufficient_data, do not invent results - tell the user what's missing.

response_metric.description: Which recovery/wellness metric to measure response in

lookback_days.description: Days of history to analyze (default 120, min 30, max 365). Longer = more events but older data may be less relevant.

tools.name: reality_check_goal
tools.description:
Reality-check an athlete's performance goal against their current fitness and training volume. Returns the athlete's PMC status, recent training trends, and a structured reference of typical adaptation rates from sports science so you can honestly tell them whether their target is realistic in the timeframe they want, and lay out two scenarios: (A) what's achievable at their current weekly hours, and (B) what's achievable if they bump volume to a specified level. ALWAYS use this tool when the athlete sets a numeric performance goal with a timeframe (e.g. "I want to go from 250W to 280W FTP in 8 weeks", "sub-3 marathon by October", "bench 100kg by summer"). Do not guess - use this so the answer is grounded in their actual data and documented adaptation rates.

Typical realistic adaptation rates for a trained but non-elite athlete (use as upper-bound reference, not promise):
- FTP / cycling threshold power: ~1-2% per week during a focused build block (3-6%/month), tapering as athlete approaches genetic ceiling. Beginners can see 5-10%/month.
- Running threshold pace / VO2max: ~1-3 sec/km improvement per week in a focused block; ~2-4% VO2max gain per 8-week block.
- 5K time: ~30-90 sec improvement over 8-12 weeks for intermediate runners on a structured plan.
- Marathon time: ~2-5% improvement per training cycle (12-16 weeks) for intermediates.
- Strength (compound lifts, intermediate): ~2.5-5kg per month on main lifts in a focused block.
- Body composition: ~0.5-1% body weight per week loss is sustainable, but only above a healthy floor. Do NOT endorse loss that pushes BMI below 19 or body fat below ~18% (female) / ~8% (male), and flag low energy availability (<30 kcal/kg fat-free mass) before recommending any further deficit. For an already-lean athlete, lead with energy availability, hormonal, and bone-health risk rather than a loss rate, and suggest a sports dietitian / physician for targets at or below BMI 18.5.
- Volume increases: cap at ~10% per week to avoid injury (acute:chronic workload ratio < 1.3).

Caveats to surface in your response: adaptation rate scales with current training age (beginners gain faster, advanced athletes plateau), recovery quality, consistency, and how close the athlete already is to their genetic ceiling. Hours/week alone is a rough proxy; intensity distribution matters as much.

goal_metric.description: What they want to improve, e.g. 'FTP', '5K time', 'marathon time', 'bench press 1RM', 'body weight'

timeframe_weeks.description: Weeks until they want to hit the target

proposed_weekly_hours.description: Optional alternative weekly hours for scenario B (if not provided, use current + ~30%)

tools.name: get_weather_forecast
tools.description: Current conditions + hourly + daily weather forecast for a location. Use this to help the athlete dress for upcoming workouts, adjust hydration/pacing for heat or cold, or plan around precipitation. Pass either {latitude, longitude} OR {location} as a place name (e.g. 'Boulder, CO'). If you don't know the user's location, check their athlete profile first; if missing, call strava_get_athlete (returns city/state/country) and pass that as the location string. Defaults to imperial units (Fahrenheit, mph, inches).

location.description: Place name to geocode (e.g. 'Boulder, CO' or 'Munich, Germany'). Used if latitude/longitude not provided.

include_hourly.description: Include hour-by-hour forecast (default true). Set false for token savings if only daily summary is needed.

tools.name: get_historical_weather
tools.description: Historical weather conditions for a date range. Use this to contextualize past workouts ('the reason that tempo run felt brutal: 88F + 70% RH') or analyze race-day conditions. Archive data lags ~2-5 days behind today, so for very recent days use get_weather_forecast instead. Pass either {latitude, longitude} or {location}.

location.description: Place name to geocode if lat/lon not provided

include_hourly.description: Include hourly data (more tokens). Default false.

tools.name: geocode_location
tools.description: Resolve a place name (e.g. 'Boulder, CO') to latitude/longitude. Useful for caching the user's coordinates in their athlete profile so future weather lookups are faster and more precise.

tools.name: terra_get_activities
tools.description: Get recent activities from a Terra-backed provider (Polar, COROS, Suunto, Zwift, Rouvy, TrainerRoad, TrainingPeaks). Reads from activity_metrics where source matches the provider key. For Strava/Garmin/Wahoo/Hevy use the dedicated provider tools instead - those return richer per-platform fields.

provider.description: Which Terra-backed activity source to read

days.description: Days back from today (default 30, max 365). Inclusive of today.

tools.name: terra_get_recent_data
tools.description: Snapshot of everything a Terra-backed provider has shipped recently: activities (if it tracks them), wellness scalars in daily_metrics, nutrition logs, cycle events. Useful when an athlete wants a 'what does Polar/COROS/Suunto know about me?' overview. For nutrition queries (Cronometer / MyFitnessPal) prefer food_log_get — it aggregates daily macro totals across all sources.

tools.name: push_workout_to_watch
tools.description: Push a structured workout straight to the athlete's watch (Garmin / COROS) for a given day, via Terra. Connected push target(s): garmin_push. The workout appears on the device as a scheduled structured workout the athlete can start with one tap. Sports that map to a device activity type push (Run / Ride / VirtualRide / Swim / Strength); Rest / Yoga / Mobility / Pilates can't be pushed and will return an error. Cycling power targets resolve to absolute watts using the athlete's FTP when known, else FTP%; running-power (Stryd) sessions use targetPowerWatts (absolute watts) and land as a native Garmin power alert. Calling twice lands two copies on the watch (no dedup) - push once per workout.

date.description: Day the workout should appear on the watch, YYYY-MM-DD.

sport.description: Run | Ride | VirtualRide | Swim | Strength. Maps to the device activity type. Rest / Yoga / Mobility / Pilates are not pushable.

title.description: Workout name shown on the watch.

description.description: Optional execution notes / intent shown with the workout.

target_load.description: Estimated TSS, attached to the workout metadata.

provider.description: Which connected push target to use (garmin_push). Omit to use the most-recently-connected one.

workout_blocks.description: Structured intervals JSON: { "blocks": [ ... ] }. Each leaf block has kind (warmup/steady/cooldown/rest), durationSec OR distanceMeters, and a target. Range targets accept a single number OR a [low,high] band (a scalar is coerced to [n,n]): targetFtpPct for cycling, targetPowerWatts absolute watts for running-power/Stryd or cycling-by-watts, targetPaceSecPerKm for running, targetHrBpm, or targetHrPctMax for HR; targetHrZone is an integer 1-5. The zone/%max forms resolve to the athlete's own watch zones on push. Interval blocks have { kind:"interval", repeats, work:{...}, rest:{...} }. Same schema as the coach's upsert_plan_session.

tools.name: delete_workout_from_watch
tools.description: Remove a previously-pushed workout from the athlete's watch (Garmin / COROS) for a given day, via Terra - the delete counterpart to push_workout_to_watch. Connected push target(s): garmin_push. Recovers the workout id(s) by reading that day's planned workouts back from Terra, so it works even for a workout pushed in an earlier session. Pass the "title" arg to remove only matching workouts (case-insensitive substring); omit it to clear every pushed workout on that date. COROS deletes reliably; a Garmin workout that has ALREADY synced to the device may still need to be removed in Garmin Connect. Confirm the date (and title, if the athlete named one) before deleting.

date.description: Day whose pushed workout(s) to remove, YYYY-MM-DD.
